step_matches.reason: Both have the requesting department nominate the cardholder.
Both have the nominee complete the initial training.
Both cover the appointing authority (HA/designee) appointing the cardholder with SF 1402.
Both suspend the account until refresher training is completed.
Both have N8 assign the appropriate LOA to the purchase request.
Both have the requestor complete the required documentation and obtain approval signatures.
No AI step covers N8 providing funds status updates from the Corporate Master Execution File; S20 only checks availability.
Both have N8 forward the requirement to the Comptroller for review.
Both have N8 ask Division Directors/Special Assistants for remaining unfunded requirements.
Both have the cardholder confirm the R/FM has committed sufficient funds.
Both have the cardholder screen the purchase against mandatory sources.
Both have the cardholder obtain AO approval before purchasing.
Both have the cardholder confirm the merchant agrees to the billing, no back-order, 30-day delivery and packing list terms.
Both have the cardholder remind the merchant not to charge sales tax.
Both have the cardholder certify that quality and quantity match the vendor agreement.
The FOB destination action was merged into AI S37, which is already matched to S14.
Both have the cardholder record the transaction in the purchase card log with documentation.
Both have the cardholder use pay-and-confirm procedures.
Both have the cardholder certify the bank statement and forward documentation to the AO/CO.
Both have the AO review the statement and documentation and certify the account for payment.
Both have the cardholder attach an explanation for undocumented transactions.
Both have the AO/CO certify the cardholder's monthly statement or invoice.
Both have the AO/CO notify the A/OPC or NETC N4 of a suspected unauthorized purchase.
Both have the AO/CO complete the PAT review and return documentation to the cardholder.
Both have the cardholder or AO contact the A/OPC about an unrecognized or suspect transaction.
Both have the cardholder dispute the transaction through CitiDirect invoice certification.
Both submit or fax the CITIBANK dispute form.
Both track the dispute to resolution.
Both offset the charge with a vendor or bank credit.
Both send the cardholder a letter explaining the decision.
Both notify the A/OPC of suspected fraud.
Both have the A/OPC contact CITIBANK about the fraud.
Both have CITIBANK close the account and issue a replacement card.
The AI assigns short-pay to the AO/CO rather than the cardholder, which is a different actor.
Both have the cardholder submit the Declaration of Unauthorized Use form to the bank.
Both have the cardholder report the lost or stolen card to CITIBANK.
Both have the cardholder notify the AO and A/OPC.
Both have the AO submit a written report to the A/OPC.
Both have CITIBANK mail a replacement card.
Both have the cardholder cut the found card in half and hand it in.
Both have the A/OPC ensure the account is inactive 30 days before departure.
Both have the A/OPC reduce limits to $1 and cut up the card.
Both have the A/OPC close the account after everything clears.
Both have the cardholder turn in GCPC transaction files to the AO/CO.

decision_matches.reason: Both test the micro-purchase threshold, and Yes leads to the SF 1402 appointment in each.
The AI has no decision on revocation, transfer, separation or retirement.
The AI tests only refresher training, and its Yes branch leads to providing a certificate rather than to purchase processing.
The conditions match, but the AI's No branch ends instead of leading to funds status updates.
The exhausted branch matches, but the AI's funds-available branch goes to LOA assignment rather than the fiscal-year-end unfunded requirements request.
Both test a fair and reasonable price, and Yes leads to the merchant terms step.
Both test billing for items not received, with Yes leading to pay-and-confirm and No to certifying the statement.
Both test cardholder availability, with Yes leading to cardholder review and No to the path where the AO certifies.
The condition is the same and the missing-documentation branch matches, but the documented branch leads to cardholder certification rather than AO/CO certification.
Both test whether the dispute was resolved for the cardholder, with Yes leading to a credit and No to a letter.
The AI decides fraud versus dispute before contacting CITIBANK, so its Yes branch leads to notification rather than account closure.
Both test whether the card is found, with Yes leading to cutting it in half.
The AI has no decision on whether the cardholder is leaving the command.
Both test for outstanding transactions, with Yes leading to reducing limits and No to closing the account.
